sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: cAMP pharmacology assay: HA-SecR pEC50 = 10.6 ± 0.2 vs WT-SecR pEC50 = 11.0 ± 0.1 (n=4); near-equivalent activity confirming functional surface expression of the tagged full-length receptor.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide of SCTR spans residues 1–22 (last residue A at position 22); the mature N-terminus begins at H23. Both PMC7435274 (L1/L2/L3) and PMC6750928 (L4/L5) replace the native signal peptide with a heterologous one and append an epitope tag (FLAG or HA) that is presented extracellularly immediately after cleavage, placing the junction at insert_after_residue=22. Python confirms residue 22 = A and residue 23 = H, consistent with the signal-peptide boundary. L3 provides direct functional validation showing near-equivalent cAMP potency (ΔpEC50 = 0.4), qualifying this as surface_and_function. The mature ECD spans 119 residues before the first TM helix (142–166), providing ample space for a short epitope tag. Full-length human SCTR with native signal peptide (residues 1–22) replaced by the HA signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope (N-terminal) and an 8×HIS tag (C-terminal, flanked by 3C cleavage sites), expressed in a mammalian system for cryo-EM structural studies (PMC7435274). A parallel study (PMC6750928) used the 5HT3a signal sequence followed by an HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) at the same N-terminal position with a C-terminal 1D4 tag, in a multiplexed GPCR panel including SCTR. Both constructs place the epitope tag immediately after signal peptide cleavage at residue 22, presenting it on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: Fig. 1 Cryo-EM structure of the secretin:SecR:DNGα s v2:Nb35 complex. a Pharmacology of the expression construct for HA-SecR versus WT-SecR (WT-SecR, pEC50 11.0 ± 0.1; HA-SecR, pEC50 10.6 ± 0.2; n = 4). b SEC trace of post FLAG-affinity column elution (left panel), the complex peak (gray, dotted lines) was isolated and used for cryo-EM imaging, with the right panel illustrating stability of the complex following one cycle of freeze-thawing. c Coomassie stain of the purified complex separated by PAGE (right panel).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines converge on a single extracellular site: the N-terminal tag placed after signal peptide cleavage at residue 22. L1 and L2 describe the construct architecture; L3 provides functional validation; L4 and L5 confirm the same N-terminal tagging strategy in a separate study. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any extracellular loop (ECL1 200–216, ECL2 277–291, ECL3 361–367) or elsewhere in the large N-terminal ECD (23–141). The C-terminal tags (8×HIS in L1–L3; 1D4 in L4–L5) are appended after residue 440, which falls within the intracellular C-tail (392–440) and therefore do not qualify as surface tag sites; they are recorded in other_positions. No transposon, domain-insertion screen, or fluorescent-protein fusion data for SCTR appear in the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 8×HIS tag (L1–L3) and 1D4 tag (L4–L5) appended after residue 440, which lies within the intracellular C-tail (topology 392–440); not accessible on the extracellular face.
